blocks.text: Felix Audit d09 — Realtime: PubSub, channels, presence, webhooks, SSE

content.value: Read-only audit against Phoenix Mastery Corpus Part VI (ch 50-53) and ch 85, using the sheets op path (2s/25-op debounced persist, {:sheets_op} deltas) as the house-good reference for every bursty producer. Method: enumerated all Phoenix.PubSub broadcast/subscribe call sites, classified topic granularity, checked subscriber-side collapse/throttle, read webhooks/ in full, and traced socket auth token discipline + SSE backpressure. Parent task task-57c1fafec69f1bd2.

Bottom line: the webhook subsystem, channel/socket auth, per-doc/per-workspace topic scoping, and inbound throttles are all already-good — genuinely hardened, not merely tidy. Two qualifying gaps, both on the SSE (ListenController) leg.

blocks.text: Finding 1 (P1) — SSE listen_loop: unbounded mailbox under a slow/stalled reader

content.value: NAMED FAILURE MODE. BarkparkWeb.ListenController.listen_loop/5 (listen_controller.ex:129-164) has no subscriber-side backpressure. The HTTP adapter is Bandit (config/config.exs:18); Plug.Conn.chunk/2 blocks the connection process on a stalled TCP reader (full send buffer / zero window). While blocked in chunk, Phoenix.PubSub.broadcast keeps send/2-ing {:document_changed, msg} into that SAME process's mailbox — each msg carries a full rendered document. On a high-mutation dataset (e.g. a bulk import at ~100 events/s) a single stalled SSE client grows the connection-process mailbox without bound: heap growth -> node memory exhaustion.

There is no message_queue_len check, no max_heap_size / off-heap guard, and no drop/collapse/close policy anywhere in lib/ (grep: 0 hits). The `after 30_000 -> keepalive` receive timeout never fires under sustained load because messages keep arriving, so the loop never yields to inspect its backlog. This is a scar-class unbounded-BEAM-mailbox footgun. Contrast the house-good sheets path which bounds the PRODUCER (debounce); the SSE consumer bounds nothing.

blocks.value:
# fix direction (delegated to the filed task)
# guard the backlog around chunk; above a threshold either
#   * drain + collapse to a single 'resync' event -> client re-pulls via Last-Event-ID, or
#   * close the stream -> client reconnects and replays
case Process.info(self(), :message_queue_len) do
  {:message_queue_len, n} when n > @backlog_max -> collapse_or_close(conn)
  _ -> chunk(conn, event)
end

content.value: Filed: task-febe33ce84d39bb4 (priority 1). Acceptance criteria carry a protective test that floods N messages at a blocked chunk sink and asserts message_queue_len stays bounded — fails today (grows to N).

blocks.text: Finding 2 (P2) — SSE live leg re-fetches get_document per event even for admin callers

content.value: MEASURED COST. redacted_result/4 (listen_controller.ex:196-208) calls Content.get_document (plus fetch_schema) for EVERY forwarded event, for EVERY subscriber, to re-seal field visibility. Correct and necessary for a redacting caller. But the controller's own comment (line 24) states an admin caller => Envelope.render/3 is a no-op => byte-identical stream, and the live broadcast msg already carries document: Envelope.render(doc, nil, :internal) — the unredacted render, current as of the just-committed mutation (broadcast.ex:133). So for an admin/unredacting caller the per-event get_document round-trip is pure overhead; its result is byte-identical to the :internal render already in hand.

Cost: N subscribers x M mutations/s => N*M redundant DB fetches during mutation bursts. Fix (field-visibility invariant preserved, fail-closed): when caller_context is admin/unredacting, forward msg.document directly; keep the re-fetch path for every redacting / owner-scoped caller. forward_event?/2 already drops cross-workspace events before the fetch, so only same-workspace admin events pay this.
Filed: task-4469f80374b0bd24 (priority 2). Acceptance criteria carry a measurement counting get_document calls per M live events for an admin subscriber (M today -> 0 after).

Webhooks (dispatcher.ex, delivery.ex, retry_worker.ex, stuck_delivery_sweeper.ex): HMAC-SHA256 signing over `timestamp.body` with an HONEST absent-header for blank secrets (never a forgeable empty-key HMAC); jittered equal-jitter backoff [1s,5s,30s] with a ceiling; retries SCHEDULED via a one-shot Oban RetryWorker fenced on updated_at (never Process.sleep in a bounded pool slot — the documented head-of-line-blocking fix); UNIQUE(endpoint_id,event_id) dedup; Retry-After honoured (clamped); SSRF guard with redirect:false; per-attempt durable state machine + crash-sweep recovery. Ordering is at-least-once with consumer-side reordering via the monotonic x-barkpark-event-id header — the Stripe model ch85 references. Nothing to add.

Socket/channel auth: UserSocket fails the connect closed on an unverifiable bearer read-token; SearchChannel re-authorizes the token against the resolved workspace on JOIN (the P0 leak guard) before any handle_in. QuizSocket uses Phoenix.Token with max_age 86_400 and server-authoritative player ids; a forged/expired token yields a fresh id. PreviewToken enforces exp + revocation + one-time jti. Token-expiry discipline is present everywhere it matters.

Inbound backpressure: PulseChannel throttles cursor frames to >=80ms (silent drop); QuizChannel throttles cursor 33ms / hover 50ms / submit 250ms per socket. Writes stay on the rate-limited HTTP POST; the sockets are subscribe-only in practice.

Topic granularity: broadcast.ex is the single owner of topic shapes; doc_topic/4 and paper_topic/3 workspace-scope every per-doc topic (barkpark-n56v / -rwva) so two tenants' colliding ids never collapse onto one topic. The bare documents:<dataset> topic fans out to all tenants only on the nil-workspace back-compat path; a resolved workspace subscribes to documents:ws:<id>:<dataset>. Subscriber-side collapse is real where it counts: chat activity broadcasts change-only (a hundred stream deltas collapse to one 'writing…'), and BoardLive dedups via a seen-set and applies in-memory (no per-event DB query). Pulse vitals broadcast on a bounded timer via Endpoint.broadcast fastlane.

Rejected-with-reason (noted, not filed): (a) studio_chat:activity is a single GLOBAL topic every Studio tab subscribes to — a minor cross-workspace wakeup + info smell — but it is change-only collapsed (low rate) and an admin/host-is-admin surface, so it does not clear the storm bar. (b) dispatch_async/5 back-compat path skips dedup and can double-deliver, but it is a documented legacy seam and every live caller threads event_id through dispatch_async/7.

MEASURED COST. redacted_result/4 (listen_controller.ex:196-208) calls Content.get_document (plus fetch_schema) for EVERY forwarded event, for EVERY subscriber, to re-seal field visibility. Correct and necessary for a redacting caller. But the controller's own comment (line 24) states an admin caller => Envelope.render/3 is a no-op => byte-identical stream, and the live broadcast msg already carries document: Envelope.render(doc, nil, :internal) — the unredacted render, current as of the just-committed mutation (broadcast.ex:133). So for an admin/unredacting caller the per-event get_document round-trip is pure overhead; its result is byte-identical to the :internal render already in hand.

Cost: N subscribers x M mutations/s => N*M redundant DB fetches during mutation bursts. Fix (field-visibility invariant preserved, fail-closed): when caller_context is admin/unredacting, forward msg.document directly; keep the re-fetch path for every redacting / owner-scoped caller. forward_event?/2 already drops cross-workspace events before the fetch, so only same-workspace admin events pay this.

Filed: task-4469f80374b0bd24 (priority 2). Acceptance criteria carry a measurement counting get_document calls per M live events for an admin subscriber (M today -> 0 after).

Already-good (evaluated, no change warranted)

Webhooks (dispatcher.ex, delivery.ex, retry_worker.ex, stuck_delivery_sweeper.ex): HMAC-SHA256 signing over `timestamp.body` with an HONEST absent-header for blank secrets (never a forgeable empty-key HMAC); jittered equal-jitter backoff [1s,5s,30s] with a ceiling; retries SCHEDULED via a one-shot Oban RetryWorker fenced on updated_at (never Process.sleep in a bounded pool slot — the documented head-of-line-blocking fix); UNIQUE(endpoint_id,event_id) dedup; Retry-After honoured (clamped); SSRF guard with redirect:false; per-attempt durable state machine + crash-sweep recovery. Ordering is at-least-once with consumer-side reordering via the monotonic x-barkpark-event-id header — the Stripe model ch85 references. Nothing to add.

Socket/channel auth: UserSocket fails the connect closed on an unverifiable bearer read-token; SearchChannel re-authorizes the token against the resolved workspace on JOIN (the P0 leak guard) before any handle_in. QuizSocket uses Phoenix.Token with max_age 86_400 and server-authoritative player ids; a forged/expired token yields a fresh id. PreviewToken enforces exp + revocation + one-time jti. Token-expiry discipline is present everywhere it matters.

Inbound backpressure: PulseChannel throttles cursor frames to >=80ms (silent drop); QuizChannel throttles cursor 33ms / hover 50ms / submit 250ms per socket. Writes stay on the rate-limited HTTP POST; the sockets are subscribe-only in practice.

Topic granularity: broadcast.ex is the single owner of topic shapes; doc_topic/4 and paper_topic/3 workspace-scope every per-doc topic (barkpark-n56v / -rwva) so two tenants' colliding ids never collapse onto one topic. The bare documents:<dataset> topic fans out to all tenants only on the nil-workspace back-compat path; a resolved workspace subscribes to documents:ws:<id>:<dataset>. Subscriber-side collapse is real where it counts: chat activity broadcasts change-only (a hundred stream deltas collapse to one 'writing…'), and BoardLive dedups via a seen-set and applies in-memory (no per-event DB query). Pulse vitals broadcast on a bounded timer via Endpoint.broadcast fastlane.

Rejected-with-reason (noted, not filed): (a) studio_chat:activity is a single GLOBAL topic every Studio tab subscribes to — a minor cross-workspace wakeup + info smell — but it is change-only collapsed (low rate) and an admin/host-is-admin surface, so it does not clear the storm bar. (b) dispatch_async/5 back-compat path skips dedup and can double-deliver, but it is a documented legacy seam and every live caller threads event_id through dispatch_async/7.
